title: Delhi. Can’t breathe. can’t move; AQI inches closer to severe
content: Delhi's air quality index is deteriorating and expected to reach severe levels by Friday. Local emissions contribute 31% while stubble burning has increased to 16.2% of total pollution. Various areas in Delhi are already experiencing severe air quality conditions. The Commission for Air Quality Management issued notices over stubble burning in Punjab districts. Weather conditions and local emissions continue to exacerbate the pollution crisis in the city.

title: 3 Naga militants killed in Manipur factional gunfight

The conflict arose after accusations were made regarding one group's collaboration with security forces. Additionally, there was gunfire directed at passenger vehicles in Ukhrul, though no injuries occurred. The Manipur government has initiated measures to restore peace through the establishment of local peace committees.

title: Watch: Hot oil spills on 3 as woman rams SUV into kebab centre in Bengaluru

The incident occurred when she felt dizzy and mistakenly pressed the accelerator instead of the brakes. Paramesh A filed a complaint after she failed to fulfill her promise to cover repair costs and medical expenses. While Safrulla Abdul Aziz claimed to have already paid approximately Rs 75,000 for the injuries, the matter remains unclear.

title: 29+ US communities curb new AI data centres; Texas elects pro-pause governor

These measures reflect a growing concern about the impact of data centres on power and water use, and noise. In Texas, the election of Gina Hinojosa as governor may lead to further restrictions on data centre construction. Meanwhile, a majority of voters in Ohio support prohibiting large facilities in their communities.

title: Chennai teen writes 160 nature poems and publishes two books before 15

Her first book, 'Dewdrops: A Gallery of Nature Poetry', debuted in 2023, followed by 'Earthen Writes: The Diary of an Earthling' in 2024. At just 15, she was honored by the India Book of Records, showcasing her profound love for the natural world through her verse.

title: Father played alongside Kapil Dev, son Jayant wants to wear India colours

title: Crude crashes below $100: Brent, WTI hit over two-month lows after midterm elections
content: Oil prices experienced a notable downturn, with Brent crude slipping below $95 and WTI declining beneath $90. This trend follows substantial losses from earlier sessions, influenced by the political shifts stemming from the US midterm elections. The election results could reshape President Donald Trump's stance towards the Iran conflict, opening doors for potential negotiations.

title: 'God help you': Shastri as Virat Kohli breaks Sachin Tendulkar's record
content: Virat Kohli made batting look easy in India's first ODI against New Zealand in Auckland on Wednesday. The star batter scored 74 runs off 51 balls to help India win the match by five wickets (DLS) and take a 1-0 lead in the five-match series. India had to chase a revised target of 143 runs in 32 overs. Kohli made sure there was no late drama as India reached the target in just 22.4 overs. Kohli hit 13 fours and a six during his innings. His shots through the covers and pulls were among the highlights of his knock.

title: 194 families assemble 4,466 acres for $1.4B data-centre deal

This ambitious $1.4 billion development will span 4,466 acres, affecting 194 families in the area. Alongside the main project, amenities such as a micro-hospital and recreational spaces are promised to enhance community welfare. However, property transfers will require further environmental assessments and reviews before finalization.

title: New Jersey woman wins $173,000 after warned-about oak tree hits home
content: In a remarkable case in New Jersey, a homeowner secured $173,000 in damages after an oak tree, reported multiple times as hazardous, fell and damaged her property. The nearby utility company was found negligent in maintaining the tree. Following a favorable jury ruling, the appeals court affirmed the decision, underscoring the obligation of the utility company to address known risks.

title: How Florida turned toy rabbits into robots to lure pythons & protect Everglades
content: Florida researchers created robotic rabbits to attract invasive Burmese pythons in the Everglades. These decoys imitate real prey by moving and generating heat, aiding in detection. The project employs remote monitoring to facilitate python removal by the South Florida Water Management District. Traditional methods relied on live rabbits, which posed logistics challenges, making robotic alternatives more practical. Current testing continues with future plans to add scent to enhance effectiveness.

title: Eiffel Tower was built to stand for only 20 years, saved by radio antenna
content: The Eiffel Tower, built in 1889 in honor of the French Revolution, faced the threat of demolition after its completion. However, thanks to Gustave Eiffel's forward-thinking design, it not only survived but thrived, becoming a crucial site for communication and scientific endeavors. Spring and autumn are the ideal seasons to experience the tower, as the weather enhances its majestic presence.

title: Patrick and Brittany Mahomes' KC Current helps 60 women find their dream dresses

The initiative welcomed 60 members of the Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Kansas City, offering them outfits for special occasions. Players Hailie Mace, Gabrielle Robinson and Nichelle Prince also joined the event, which focused on confidence and self-expression.

title: Tom Brady and Gisele Bündchen turned $4.5M land into a $39.5M luxury mansion

They listed the estate for $39.5 million in August 2019 before reducing the asking price to $33.9 million. However, the property failed to sell and was withdrawn in May 2020 amid the coronavirus pandemic and its impact on luxury real estate.

title: 2 Naga outfits clashed over one's ties with security forces
content:
The gunfight at Taodaijang village in Noney involved militants of Zeliangrong United Front-Jenchui (ZUF-J) and Zeliangrong United Front-Kamson (ZUF-K), the latter backed by NSCN-IM. Two of the dead belonged to ZUF-J, a signatory to the cessation of operations (CoO) agreement with Centre since 2022, and the third to ZUF-K. The trigger for the clash was purportedly a statement from ZUF-K on Nov 1, accusing ZUF-J of betraying the Naga by hobnobbing with security forces. In Kangpokpi district, Committee on Tribal Unity, Sadar Hills, extended its shutdown by 48 hours, until 5 pm on Nov 6, after accusing the govt of failing to identify who abducted and killed two Kuki-Zo tribesmen last week. The fresh turmoil comes a day after chief minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh directed security agencies to identify "active" armed groups, excluding those engaged in peace talks with the state govt.
